sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri R. B. Singh, Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Tarun Pagare, Government Advocate for the non-ap  ORDER
Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is first application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of bail relating to FIR/Crime No.502/2022 dated (not mentioned)
registered at Police Station Taal, District Ratlam (M.P.) for the offence u/S 363, 363/34, 366,
366/34 and 376(2)(n) of IPC alongwith Section 5(l)/6 of the POCSO Act and 3(2)(v) and 3(1)(w)(i)
of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

Applicant is in custody since 15.11.2022.
2.
As per prosecution story, it is alleged that applicant has committed rape upon the prosecutrix.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is submitted that prosecutrix is a consenting party.
Certainly, age of the prosecutrix is 17 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:12107 2 MCRC-17443-2025 years.
However, in her statement recorded u/S 164 of Cr.P.C., she has not supported the case of prosecution and has clearly stated that applicant has not used force.

It is also pointed out in her statement recorded before the Court that last time she has again stated that it is true to say that she came in the Court with her father and stated things at the instructions of her father.
Applicant is having no criminal past.

Applicant is a young boy of 20 years and is in custody since 15.11.2022 i.e.
Mahesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108451855/
1 more than 2.5 years.

sentences.text: It is submitted that keeping the applicant in further custody will ruin his career.
Final conclusion of trial will take sufficient long time.
Under these circumstances, counsel prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
4. On the other hand, learned Government Advocate opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection but has fairly admitted that the applicant is having no previous criminal records.

5. Having considered the rival submissions and looking to overall facts and circumstances of the case as well as custody period and age of applicant, I am of the view that it is a case, in which applicant may be released on bail.
Consequently without commenting on the merits of the case, this bail application stands allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant/accused be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for securing his presence before the said Court on all the dates of hearing fixed in this regard during trial.
It is also directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of the BNSS.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:12107 3 MCRC-17443-2025 7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
8. With the aforesaid, this application is allowed and stands disposed of.
Certified copy, as per Rules.

(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) JUDGE gp Mahesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108451855/
